data.summary: Pacman moving directly onto a ghost's current tile can miss the collision entirely because the collision check runs only once, after both pacman and the ghost have moved that tick.
data.why: State where pacman at (5,5) and a chasing ghost at (6,5) (adjacent, ghost's `home`/mode irrelevant). Player presses 'right': attemptMove doesn't treat ghost-occupied tiles as blocked, so pacman.pos becomes (6,5) — the ghost's own pre-move tile. Then moveGhosts runs with target = pacman's NEW pos (6,5), which is exactly where the ghost already sits, so Manhattan distance from any of its walkable neighbors to that target is always 1 (tied), and moveGhost always picks one of those neighbors (there's no 'stay' option), moving the ghost off (6,5) to e.g. (6,4). resolveGhostCollisions then compares final positions (6,5) vs (6,4): no collision, no life lost. The same logic means a frightened ghost that pacman moves onto is also missed for the 'eaten for points' case (CAP-1.4), since the frightened ghost likewise always steps away when its target-distance-to-self is 0. This reproduces on essentially every head-on approach where the ghost has at least one open non-reverse neighbor, i.e. most of normal play, not a rare corner case.

data.summary: The ghost chase/flee pathing (src/game.ts#moveGhost, moveGhosts, tick) that drives every frame's ghost movement has no CAP-1.x criterion or pointer at all.
data.why: CAP-1 would need a criterion (e.g. 'ghosts advance one step per tick toward/away from pacman') bound to a test id and pointing at src/game.ts#moveGhost/tick, since this is core gameplay behavior explicitly called out in SEAL.md ('four ghosts sharing one chase/flee AI') but is untouched by any existing criterion (CAP-1.4 only covers collision resolution, not movement).

data.summary: New src/render.ts (drawFrame, drawPacman, drawGhost, TILE) implements the pixel-art rendering CAP-1.8 describes, but CAP-1.8's pointer only names src/main.ts#applyScale.
data.why: CAP-1.8 talks about the canvas 'keeping the maze's aspect ratio and pixel-art sharpness' — the sharpness/drawing half of that is implemented entirely in the new src/render.ts module, which needs its own pointer (or criterion) rather than being covered implicitly by applyScale.

data.text: Fixed the blocking correctness finding by resolving ghost collisions twice per tick in src/game.ts#tick: once immediately after pacman moves (catches pacman stepping onto a ghost's pre-move tile, chasing or frightened) and again after the ghosts move (catches a ghost stepping onto pacman) — was previously checked only once, after both had moved, so head-on approaches were missed.

Added CAP-1.9 ('each tick, every ghost advances one walkable step toward pacman when chasing and away when frightened') to canon/capabilities/CAP-1.md, bound to new coverage row P0-GAME-008, pointing at src/game.ts#moveGhost and #moveGhosts, with `// canon: CAP-1.9` tags on both, answering the finding that ghost pathing carried no criterion.
Added src/render.ts#drawFrame as a second pointer on CAP-1.8 (with a `// canon: CAP-1.8` tag) since the pixel-art sharpness half of that criterion lives in render.ts, not only main.ts#applyScale.

Added regression tests under P0-GAME-004 in src/game.test.ts proving same-tick pacman-onto-ghost collisions are now caught (both the chasing-ghost life-loss case and the frightened-ghost eaten-for-points case), and new tests under P0-GAME-008 proving a ghost steps toward pacman while chasing and away while frightened.

data.summary: In tick(), a frightened ghost forced to step onto pacman's tile (e.g. a dead-end with only that walkable neighbor) can be resolved as a chase-mode collision instead of being eaten, if that same tick is when frightenedTicks counts down to 0.
data.why: State: frightenedTicks=1 entering tick, a ghost in mode 'frightened' has only one walkable neighbor and it happens to be pacman's tile (nonReverse pool empty so the reversal-into-pacman option is used). tick() computes moveGhosts() while the ghost is still mode='frightened' (so it lands on pacman's tile as the forced 'flee' step), then immediately does `frightenedTicks = Math.max(0, afterGhosts.frightenedTicks - 1)` -> 0, and maps every ghost's mode to 'chase' *before* calling the second resolveGhostCollisions(). resolveGhostCollisions() then sees mode==='chase' for the ghost sitting on pacman and calls loseLife() (costing a life) instead of the frightened branch (eaten for +200 points), even though the collision was produced by frightened-mode movement in this same tick.

data.summary: resolveGhostCollisions only resolves the first ghost found on pacman's tile via Array.find, so if two ghosts simultaneously occupy pacman's tile in the same tick, only one collision is processed.
data.why: State where two ghosts' independent moveGhost() results both land on pacman's position in the same moveGhosts() call (e.g. two ghosts approaching from different directions with the same Manhattan-shortest tile); `state.ghosts.find(...)` returns only the first array match, so if that first ghost is frightened (removed/scored) or a chase ghost causing loseLife+respawn, the second overlapping ghost's simultaneous presence on pacman's tile is never separately checked that tick.

data.summary: src/main.ts's render() now writes score, lives, and win/lose status text to the DOM (#score, #lives, #status), but no CAP-1.x criterion, binding, or pointer covers this HUD/status display behaviour.
data.why: CAP-1.5 and CAP-1.6 only describe the win/lose state transition (pointing at checkWin/loseLife), not the observable behaviour of displaying 'You win!'/'Game over' or the live score/lives text; a criterion (or pointer on an existing one) naming src/main.ts's render function is needed.

data.summary: tick() in src/game.ts now counts down frightenedTicks each tick and reverts every ghost from 'frightened' back to 'chase' once it hits zero, but no criterion describes this expiry, only the onset (CAP-1.3, pointing at eatDot).
data.why: CAP-1.3's pointer (src/game.ts#eatDot) only covers a pellet frightening ghosts, not the new timed reversion logic added in tick(); a criterion or an additional pointer on src/game.ts#tick for the frightened-duration countdown is missing.
